title: Architect Evidence Slab and Customer Storyline
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Executive summary:

This page provides a compact, architect-focused evidence slab and customer storyline designed for technical GTM: a single-page narrative, a 15-slide pitch outline, battle-tested rebuttals, price guidance for pilot-to-scale, a short anonymous case study, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this when engaging platform or infra architects who need measurable economics, latency guarantees, and a migration path that minimizes engineering lift.

Goal: help field and SA teams convert technical validation into procurement signals within 8–12 weeks.

Key positioning statements (for architects and platform teams):
- Redwood Inference is a delivery-first inference platform: same API, same observability, three deployment modes (Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, Private VPC/on-prem) so you can start fast and graduate to isolation without rewriting integrations.
- Predictable economics through explicit batching, KV cache, and routing policies—customers see 2x–5x cost improvement vs unmanaged GPU endpoints for typical chat workloads.
- Reliability-first: routing fallbacks and model variants keep critical APIs online during capacity events.
- Security posture: KMS/HSM-ready for key isolation, VPC peering or private-link, and audit logging across all deployment modes.

One-line value prop for slides:
"Ship dependable LLM features fast, control cost at scale, keep the same API whether hosted or on customer VPC."

Competitive brief (concise):
- Primary competitors to surface:
  - CloudServe AI (large cloud provider managed endpoints): strongest on raw infrastructure scale and ecosystem integrations; weaker on transparent per-token economics, and slower to provide rollout tooling tied to model quality.
  - EdgeHost / OpenFan runtimes (open-source runtimes + infra): strong customization and lower per-hour cost at large scale, but heavy ops burden, no centralized model catalog, and limited customer-facing observability.
  - BlackBox LLM API (single-tenant API vendors): easy to use but limited deployment modes and expensive at scale; often no private deployment option.

Positioning vs competitors (what to emphasize):
- Emphasize the unified API and observability across deployment modes — reduces integration cost and risk for product teams.
- Emphasize cost controls: batching policies, quantization profiles, prefix caching yield measurable unit-cost reductions you can show in POC.
- Emphasize operational tooling: rollouts (canary, A/B, automatic fallback) and prompt/eval-linked quality monitors to avoid regressions during model swaps.

Quick battlecard (objections + scripts):
- "We can just run the open-source runtime ourselves."
  - Script: "You can, and many teams do. The hard part is shipping predictable SLAs, observability that ties cost to token-level traces, and automated rollback/rollout tooling. In our experience customers spend 3–6 months building those features and still lack the cost transparency Redwood provides out of the box."
- "Cloud provider managed endpoints are simpler."
  - Script: "Managed endpoints are fine for experimentation, but we help teams control unit economics and provide private deployment options with the same API surface—critical when data residency or auditability is required."
- "Pricing is too high for long-tail inference."
  - Script: "We offer Dedicated reserved capacity and private deployment pricing that matches expected throughput. Our Optimize toolkit will reduce token costs via batching/quantization—typically 30–60% lower unit costs compared to naive endpoints during pilot-to-scale."

Pitch deck: 15-slide outline (engineer-focused):
1) Title + 1-line value prop
2) The problem (latency unpredictability, exploding costs, ops toil)
3) Why existing options fall short (managed endpoints vs self-hosted tradeoffs)
4) Redwood solution overview (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
5) Runtime architecture highlights (kernel selection, batching, KV cache)
6) Observable economics (what we measure: token cost, per-route latency, 99th pct tail)
7) SLOs and operational guarantees (sample SLOs below)
8) Pilot plan (3–8 week technical pilot: integration, load profile, evals)
9) Pricing and commitment options (pilot vs committed capacity)
10) Case study (summary of results)
11) Security & compliance (KMS, VPC, audit logs)
12) Migration path (start hosted, move to private/dedicated)
13) Typical ROI math (sample table)
14) Risks and mitigations (fallbacks, canaries)
15) Ask & next steps (POC kickoff checklist)

Sample SLOs (copyable into security/ops decks):
- 99th percentile tail latency (text-generation, 256-token average): <= 350 ms (hosted API, Tier-1 model).
- Throughput availability (Dedicated pool): 99.95% monthly uptime for provisioned capacity.
- Cost variance: per-token cost variance <= 8% week-over-week once autoscaling config is stable.
- Audit retention: request/response logs retained for 90 days (configurable up to customer SLA).

Pilot-to-scale pricing guidance (rules of thumb):
- Pilot (0–2M tokens/day): use Hosted API with Developer tier; focus on integration and latency profiles.
- Scale evaluation (2–20M tokens/day): test Dedicated reserved pools with a 3-month commit; expect 30–45% unit cost reduction vs Hosted API for stable traffic due to reserved capacity and optimized batching.
- Enterprise scale (>20M tokens/day): move to Dedicated or Private; negotiate blended pricing including support and Optimize advisory.

Representative pricing table (example scenarios — replace with current quotes during deals):
- Hosted API: $0.0009 / token (interactive chat median) — pilot-friendly, no infra commitment.
- Dedicated (reserved): starting at $25k/month per GPU node equivalent (committed tier) + $0.0004 / token estimate depending on batching/quantization.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): license + deployment fee + runbook support; contact sales for customized quote.

Case study (anonymous, productionized):
- Customer profile: "NorthStar Retail" (global ecommerce platform, 350M monthly sessions).
- Objective: deploy personalized product assistant that reduces cart abandonment during peak traffic.
- Pilot scope: Hosted API integration for 6 weeks, 10k concurrent users simulated, SKU-level personalization prompts with 128-token average responses.
- Results: median latency 180ms, p99 310ms; per-conversation cost 48% lower after batching and KV prefix caching compared to customer's prior managed endpoints; pilot converted to Dedicated pool with 3-month commit.
- Business impact: 3.1% reduction in cart abandonment in A/B test; estimated incremental monthly GMV of $540k; payback on Dedicated commit within 2 months.
- Technical takeaways: inexpensive wins came from tuning batch target and caching cold-start prompts, and from using model variants for cold-tier traffic.

POC checklist (technical):
1) Provide API keys and sample prompts (customer)
2) Configure route with target SLO and optional prefix caching
3) Run synthetic load: 3–5 traffic patterns (burst, steady, cold-start)
4) Evaluate token-level cost and latency traces (use Redwood Console dashboards)
5) Run prompt-evals (quality guardrails) for top 50 prompt templates
6) Decision gate: if p99 <= target and unit economics within 30% of target, proceed to Dedicated sizing exercise

Security FAQ (prospect-facing short answers):
Q: How do you separate customer data in hosted mode?
A: Requests and models are isolated at the request layer, and logs can be segregated by tenant. For customers requiring stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments with dedicated pools and VPC connections.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys?
A: Yes — Redwood supports KMS integrations and can integrate with cloud-managed KMS or bring-your-own HSM for private deployments.

Q: What audit capabilities exist?
A: Request and response logging, token-level billing traces, and role-based access logs are available. Retention is configurable; default retention for audit logs is 90 days, extendable for enterprise SLAs.

Q: How do you prevent data leakage between tenants?
A: Multi-tenant isolation is enforced in the runtime (per-request memory boundaries and tenant-specific caches). For the highest assurance, Dedicated pools and Private deployments provide compute-level separation.

Q: How are CVEs and runtime vulnerabilities handled?
A: We follow a 30/90 patch SLAs policy: critical patches (CVSS >=9) are remediated within 30 days for Hosted; Dedicated and Private customers are provided a remediation plan and optional managed patch windows per contract.

Rebuttals for security teams:
- For teams demanding encryption-in-use, propose a Private deployment with HSM-backed keys and ensure network isolation via VPC and private-link.
- For teams with strict retention rules, propose extended retention and export workflows or customer-managed archival.

Common integration pitfalls & mitigations (operational):
- Overbroad prompt templates increase token count — mitigation: instrument prompt templates and set guardrails with prompt-level token caps.
- Cold cache churn on low-cardinality prompts causes latency spikes — mitigation: enable prefix/KV caching and warm caches as part of onboarding traffic simulation.

Appendix: quick ROI workbook (text table — replace numbers during qualification)
- Inputs: avg tokens per interaction, interactions/day, $/token (estimate), expected reduction from caching/batching
- Example calculation (monthly):
  - Baseline cost = interactions/day * tokens/interaction * 30 * $hosted_token
  - Optimized cost = Baseline cost * (1 - caching_reduction) * (1 - quant_reduction)

Sample next steps (sales engineer checklist):
1) Send this slab + 15-slide outline to prospect architect and ask for top 3 technical risks
2) Propose 6-week pilot: integration sprint (1 week), load testing (2 weeks), quality evals (1 week), tuning & findings (2 weeks)
3) Create a shared dashboard with customer: token costs, latency histograms, route-level traces
4) Schedule an executive review with finance and security to review pilot results and contract terms
